tools.name: update_article
tools.description: Updates an article summary, content, or parent. Content replaces the existing content unless `append` is true. Returns the article ID and URL.

articleId.description: The ID of the article to update (e.g., DEMO-A-123).

content.description: The article content in Markdown. If append is true, this will be added to the end of the existing content. Otherwise, it will completely rewrite it.

append.description: If true, the provided content will be appended to the end of the existing article content instead of overwriting it. Default is false.

parentArticleId.description: The ID of the parent article (e.g., DEMO-A-123).

tools.name: update_issue
tools.description:
Partially updates an issue or draft. Supported changes are:
- 'summary' or 'description' arguments to update only the issue summary or description.
- 'customFields' argument as key-value JSON object to update issue fields like State, Type, Priority, etc. Available 'customFields' and their possible values are listed in the issue fields schema.
- 'subscription' argument to star (true) or unstar (false) the issue on behalf of the current user. The current user is notified about subsequent issue updates according to their subscription settings for the Star tag.
- 'vote' argument to vote (true) or remove a vote (false) on behalf of the current user for the issue.
This operation cannot update issue visibility.
Returns the issue ID and a summary of applied changes.

issueId.description: The ID of the issue (for example, DEMO-123) or issue draft (for example, 3-22).

summary.description: The revised issue summary. If undefined, the existing summary remains unchanged.

description.description: The revised issue description. Draft descriptions may already contain a project template; preserve its required structure when updating it. If undefined, the existing description remains unchanged.

customFields.description: Subset of custom fields to update. Pass only fields and values that require updates; other fields will remain unchanged. Use null to clear a single-value field and an empty array to clear a multi-value field. For example, {"Type": "Task", "Priority": "Minor"}.

subscription.description: An optional flag for subscribing to or unsubscribing from issue updates (using the Star tag).

vote.description: An optional flag to add votes to or remove votes from the issue.

tools.name: log_work
tools.description: Adds a work item (spent time) to an issue. Duration is required; date, work type, description, and work item attributes are optional. Available work types and attributes are defined in the project time-tracking settings.

issueId.description: The ID of the issue that the work item belongs to.

date.description: Optional date assigned to the work item. Accepts a date string in "yyyy-MM-dd" format (e.g., 2025-08-20).

workType.description: Optional work item type name available in the project (for example, Development, Testing).

workItemAttributes.description: Optional key-value object of work item attributes assigned to the new work item. Keys are attribute names and values are one of the available options. The list of available keys and values is defined in the target project time-tracking settings.

tools.name: manage_issue_tags
tools.description: Adds a tag to or removes a tag from an issue. Tags can be identified by ID or exact name; inaccessible or unknown tags produce an error with similar-name suggestions. Returns the issue ID and updated tags.

tag.description: The ID (preferable) or name of the tag to add.

operation.description: The operation to perform: add or remove.

annotations.title: Add or remove tag from issue

tools.name: search_articles
tools.description:
Searches for Knowledge Base articles using YouTrack’s query language. The 'query' can combine attribute filters, keywords, and free text. Examples of common patterns include:

- Free text: Find matching words in the article summary (title) and content. Use single quotes for exact phrases (e.g., 'installation guide'). Wildcards: '*' matches zero or more characters. Examples: 'deployment', '"getting started"', 'guide*'.
- Project filter: 'project: <ProjectName>'. Use project name or short name. Examples: 'project: {Mobile App}', 'project: HELP'.
- Author/Updater filters: 'author: <login>' (creator) or 'updated by: <login>'. Use 'me' for the currently authenticated user. Examples: 'author: me', 'updated by: admin'.
- Tag filter: 'tag: <TagName>'. Wrap multi-word tags in braces { }. Examples: 'tag: faq', 'tag: {internal docs}'.
- Date filters: 'created:', 'updated:'. Use a date, range '..', or relative period. Relative periods: 'today', 'yesterday', '{This week}', '{Last month}', etc. Examples: 'updated: today', 'created: {This month}', 'updated: 2024-01-01 .. 2024-12-31'.
- Content/Presence filters: Use 'has: <attribute>'. Examples: 'has: attachments' (articles with files), 'has: comments', 'has: content' (non-empty articles), 'has: star' (starred by current user).
- Negation: Use '-' to exclude values. Examples: 'tag: -outdated', 'project: -{Archived}'.
- Combining filters: List multiple conditions separated by spaces (logical AND). Examples: 'project: HELP author: me has: -comments' (Articles in HELP project created by me with no comments).

Returns basic info: id, summary, url, parent article, and the content lines where the query was found. For full details, retrieve the article separately. The response is paginated using the specified offset and limit.

query.description: The search query in YouTrack syntax.

offset.description: The number of articles to skip. Default is 0.

limit.description: The maximum number of articles to return. Default is 10.

tools.name: search_issues
tools.description:
Searches for issues using YouTrack’s query language. The 'query' can combine attribute filters, keywords, and free text. Examples of common patterns include:

- Free text: Find matching words in the issue summary, description, and comments. Use wildcards: '*' for any characters, '?' for single characters (e.g., 'summary: log*', 'fix??'). Examples: 'login button bug', 'some other text', 'summary: log*', 'description: fix??'.
- Linked issues: '<linkType>: <issueId>' (by link type), 'links: <issueId>' (all linked to issueId issues). Examples: 'relates to: DEMO-123', 'subtask of: DEMO-123' (issues where DEMO-123 is a parent), 'links: DEMO-12' (issues linked to DEMO-12 with any link type). Detailed issue information includes the 'linkedIssueCounts' property, which shows the available link types for the issue.
- Issues where an issue is mentioned: 'mentions: <issueId>'. Examples: 'mentions: DEMO-123'.
- Project filter: 'project: <ProjectName>'. Use project name or project key. Examples: 'project: {Mobile App}', 'project: MA'.
- Assignee filter: 'for: <login>'. Use 'me' for the currently authenticated user. Examples: 'for: me', 'for: john.smith'.
- Reporter filter: 'reporter: <login>'. Use 'me' for the currently authenticated user. Examples: 'reporter: me', 'reporter: admin'.
- Tag filter: 'tag: <TagName>'. Wrap multi-word tags in braces { }. Examples: 'tag: urgent', 'tag: {customer feedback}'.
- Field filter: '<FieldName>: <Value>'. For any project field, for example, State, Type, Priority, and so on. Wrap multi-word names or values in { }. Possible fields and values for project issues are available in the project details. Use '-' as 'not', e.g., 'State: -Fixed' filters out fixed issues. Examples: 'Priority: High', 'State: {In Progress}, Fixed' (searches issues with 'In Progress' state + issues with 'Fixed' state), 'Due Date: {plus 5d}' (issues that are due in five days).
- Date filters: 'created:', 'updated:', 'resolved date:' (or any date field) plus a date, range, or relative period. Relative periods: 'today', 'yesterday', '{This week}', '{Last week}', '{This month}', etc. Examples: 'created: {This month}', 'updated: today', 'resolved date: 2025-06-01 .. 2025-06-30', 'updated: {minus 2h} .. *' (issues updated last 2 hours), 'created: * .. {minus 1y 6M}' (issues that are at least one and a half years old).
- Keywords: '#Unresolved' to find unresolved issues based on the State; '#Resolved' to find resolved issues.
- Empty/Non-Empty Fields: Use the 'has: <attribute>'. Example: 'has: attachments' finds issues with attachments, while 'has: -comments' finds issues with no comments. Other attributes: 'links', '<linkType>' (e.g. 'has: {subtask of}'), 'star' (subscription), 'votes', 'work'.
- Combining filters: List multiple conditions separated by spaces (logical AND). For OR operator, add it explicitly. Examples: '(project: MA) and (for: me) and (created: {minus 8h} .. *) and runtime error' (issues in project MA and assigned to currently authenticated user and created during last 8h and contains 'runtime error' text), '(Type: Task and State: Open) or (Type: Bug and Priority: Critical)'.

Returns basic info: id, summary, project, resolved, reporter, created, updated and default custom fields. For full details, retrieve the issue separately. The response is paginated using the specified offset and limit.

customFieldsToReturn.description: List of custom field names to include in the 'customFields' map. Default: ['Type','State','Assignee']. All available custom field names are listed in the issue fields schema. If empty array, include none.

limit.description: Maximum number of issues to return.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Returns project details, team information, and time-tracking settings. Available work item types and attribute values are included in the time-tracking settings.

projectKey.description: The project key. For example, DEMO.

tools.name: get_saved_issue_searches
tools.description: Returns saved searches marked as favorites by the current user. The output search queries can be used in issue searches. The response is paginated using the specified offset and/or limit.

limit.description: Maximum number of searches to return.

tools.name: get_user_group_members
tools.description: Lists users who are members of a specified group or project team. Project teams are essentially groups that are always associated with a specific project. The response is paginated using the specified offset and/or limit.

group.description: Name of the group or project team.

annotations.title: Get user group or team members

tools.name: link_issues

targetIssueId.description: The ID of the target issue or issue draft.

linkType.description: The inward or outward name of the link type. For example, "relates to", "subtask of", "depends on", "duplicates", "blocked by".

issueToLinkId.description: The ID of the issue or issue draft to link from.

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Returns details about the currently authenticated user (me): login, email, full name, time zone.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Returns an issue or draft with its summary, description, URL, project, reporter, links, attachments, tags, votes, recent comments, and visible custom fields. For drafts, the description includes any issue template applied by project workflows. The `customFields` property provides important issue details such as Type, State, Assignee, Priority, and Subsystem. Available custom fields and values are defined in the issue fields schema.

issueId.description: The ID of the issue (for example, DEMO-123) or issue draft (for example, 3-22).

recentCommentsCount.description: The number of recent comments to return in the response. Default is 5.

tools.name: get_issue_comments
tools.description: Returns issue comments with authors, text, timestamps, and attachments, paginated by offset and limit.

limit.description: Maximum number of comments to return.

tools.name: get_issue_fields_schema
tools.description: Returns the JSON schema for custom fields in the specified project, including relevant fields and values for issue creation and update actions.

projectKey.description: The project key. For example, DEMO.

tools.name: find_projects
tools.description: Finds projects whose names or keys contain a substring (case-insensitive). Returns project keys and names, paginated by offset and limit.

query.description: Substring to match in the project name or key (case-insensitive). To list all projects, use an empty string.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return.

tools.name: find_user
tools.description: Finds a user by exact login or email and returns their login, full name, email, and local time zone. The value `me` identifies the current user.

loginOrEmail.description: Username or email. When `me`, returns the currently authenticated user.

tools.name: find_user_groups
tools.description: Finds user groups or project teams whose names contain the specified substring (case-insensitive). The response is paginated using the specified offset and/or limit.

nameContains.description: Substring to match in the group or team name (case-insensitive). To list all groups and teams, use an empty string.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: Returns detailed information for an article, including summary (title), content, sub-articles, tags, and visibility settings. Supports line-by-line scrolling for long articles.

articleId.description: The ID of the article to retrieve (e.g., DEMO-A-123).

linesOffset.description: The number of lines to skip from the beginning of the article content. Default is 0.

linesCount.description: The maximum number of lines of the article content to return. Default is 500.

tools.name: create_article
tools.description: Creates an article in a project, optionally as a sub-article or with visibility restricted to specified users or groups. Returns the article ID and URL.

project.description: The key of the project where the article will be created.

parentArticle.description: The ID of an optional parent article (e.g., DEMO-A-123). The new article will be created as a child of this parent article.

permittedUsers.description: A list of logins (usernames) belonging to users who can see the article.

permittedGroups.description: A list of names belonging to groups whose members can see the article.

tools.name: create_draft_issue
tools.description: Creates an issue draft in the specified project. Project workflows may initialize the draft description from an issue template. Drafts are visible only to the current user and can be updated later. Returns the draft ID and URL.

project.description: The key of the project where the issue draft will be created.

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description: Creates an issue in the specified project. Projects may require `customFields` at creation; required fields and permitted values are available in the issue fields schema. Visibility can be restricted to specified users or groups. Returns the issue ID and URL.

project.description: The key of the project where the issue will be created.

description.description: The issue description in plain text or Markdown.

customFields.description: The custom fields where you want to set values for the new issue. Pass the field names the values you want to set. Example: {"Type": "Task", "Priority": "Minor"}.

parentIssue.description: The ID of an optional parent issue. The new issue will be linked as a subtask of the specified parent issue. Use only when specifically creating an issue as a subtask.

permittedUsers.description: A list of logins (usernames) belonging to users who can see the issue.

permittedGroups.description: A list of names belonging to groups whose members can see the issue.

tools.name: add_issue_comment
tools.description: Adds a Markdown comment to an issue, optionally restricted to specified users or groups.

text.description: The comment in plain text or Markdown.

permittedUsers.description: A list of logins (usernames) belonging to users who can see the comment.

permittedGroups.description: A list of names belonging to groups whose members can see the comment.

tools.name: change_issue_assignee
tools.description: Sets the value for the Assignee field in an issue to the specified user. If the `assigneeLogin` argument is `null`, the issue will be unassigned.

assigneeLogin.description: The login of the new assignee. If `null` or omitted, the issue will be unassigned.
